transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... honestly, I need someone to understand what's been going on at my apartment. For months now, the property manager and certain people in the building have been trying to pressure me out. It's not just a feeling, it's a clear pattern. They use misdelivered mail, and there are these timed noises in the walls... right when I'm trying to concentrate or sleep. And then there are the little comments from neighbors, just passing by, that make it obvious they're in on it. The management keeps showing me paperwork and giving me explanations, but none of it changes the pattern I can see right in front of me. They're trying to force me out.
Have you used any drugs, alcohol, or new medications around the time these experiences started?

No, nothing like that. I don't use any drugs, and I... well, I rarely even drink alcohol. As for medications, no, I haven't started anything new at all. I understand why you'd ask, but my mind is completely clear. What's happening at the apartment isn't because of something I took.
About how long have these experiences been going on?
It's been about 11 months now. It started... well, shortly after I moved into this new apartment.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you could not hear?

No, I haven't heard anything like that. The noises I hear—the banging in the walls, the footsteps—they're real sounds. Anyone standing in my living room would hear them just the same. I don't hear voices in my head or anything that isn't actually there. It's just the people in my building making sure I hear them.
Have you become noticeably more withdrawn from other people since this started?

Well, yes, I suppose I have. I've actually pulled back from several of my consulting jobs lately. I just... I spend much of my week following up with the neighbors, the management offices, and the building staff. Because of all that, I haven't really been able to settle into my normal work, or even my usual painting routine. So, I guess I am spending less time with the people I normally would, just because I have to deal with this.
Have you noticed any decline in your motivation or ability to feel pleasure since this started?

No, I wouldn't say that. I still enjoy the things I've always enjoyed. I still very much want to paint, and I still care about my consulting work. My motivation hasn't gone away at all. 

It's just that... well, my time is completely taken up by dealing with what's going on in the building. If they would just leave me be, I'd be right back to my normal routine. So, no, I haven't lost the ability to enjoy my life or anything like that. I'm just being prevented from living it normally right now.
Have you noticed your thoughts ever becoming jumbled or hard for other people to follow when you speak?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My thoughts are perfectly clear. I mean, I know exactly what I want to say and I say it. No one has ever told me I'm hard to follow or that my words don't make sense. I'm just trying to explain a complicated situation with the building, but my thinking is as sharp as it's always been.
Have you ever had a head injury, stroke, seizure disorder, or other brain illness before these apartment experiences began?

No, nothing like that. I've never had a head injury, no strokes, no seizures, or anything wrong with my brain. My physical health has always been fine. It's just this situation with the building that's the problem, not my health.
Have you ever had a period of several days or more when you felt unusually energized or irritable and needed much less sleep than usual?

No, I haven't. I've always been a pretty steady sleeper, getting my usual seven or eight hours. I haven't had any times where I felt, you know, overly energized or irritable like you're describing. The only time my sleep gets interrupted is when the noise starts up from the other apartments, but that's just because they're keeping me awake, not because I don't need the sleep.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

No, not really. I mean, I get frustrated, sure. Anyone would be stressed out dealing with what they're doing in this building. But I haven't been depressed or sitting around feeling sad all day. I just want the situation resolved so I can go back to my normal life.
Have you ever had experiences where you believed things were being controlled, inserted, or broadcast into your mind?

No, absolutely not. I don't have anyone controlling my thoughts or putting things in my head, or... broadcasting anything. My mind is my own. I know exactly what I'm thinking. Like I said, the only issue here is what the people in the building are actually doing, physically, to harass me. It has nothing to do with my mind being messed with.
Did these beliefs and experiences begin suddenly, over a period of days or weeks, rather than developing gradually?

No, it wasn't sudden. It wasn't like I woke up one morning and all this was happening. It started out... well, just small things, you know? A noise here, a comment there, maybe a few months ago. I didn't think much of it at first. But then it just kept building up, piece by piece, until it became obvious what they were doing. So, no, it wasn't overnight. It was gradual.
Have you ever been told that your speech becomes hard to follow or that your thoughts seem disorganized when you talk?

No, I haven't. Nobody has ever told me that. I communicate clearly—it's part of my job, actually, being an analyst. I need to be precise. So, no, my thoughts aren't disorganized, and I don't have trouble making myself understood. If people aren't following me, it's because they aren't listening, not because I'm not making sense.
Have you noticed that your emotions feel flatter or less expressive than they used to?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My emotions are just fine. I mean, I get angry and frustrated about what the people in the building are doing to me, which is a perfectly normal reaction to being harassed. But no, I don't feel flat or less expressive. I feel things the same way I always have.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually high, expansive, or very irritable and full of energy?

No, I haven't. I don't get unusually high or anything like that. I have a normal amount of energy, I suppose. I mean, I'm 65, I'm not bouncing off the walls. I just go to work, do my job, and try to deal with the situation in my building. So no, no periods of feeling overly energetic or expansive.
Have you ever been diagnosed with a neurological or other medical illness that could affect your thinking, such as Parkinson’s disease, dementia, epilepsy, or a stroke?

No, nothing like that. I go to my doctor for my regular checkups, and my health is fine. I don't have Parkinson's or dementia or anything that would mess with my brain. My mind is perfectly sharp. I just want the harassment to stop, that's all. But medically, neurologically, I'm completely fine.
Have these beliefs about the people in your building been present continuously for at least one month?

Yes, well over a month. It's... it's actually been going on for about 11 months now. It started shortly after I moved into the new apartment, and it hasn't stopped since. So yes, continuously for almost a year.
